name: Operations Data and Privacy
title: Operations Data and Privacy
answer: Operations systems such as transportation, food service and health records hold sensitive student information, and every tool that touches that data needs the same privacy protections as classroom tools. This matters because operations contracts are often handled by different offices than instructional ones, so privacy review can be skipped entirely. The district's privacy lead should review every contract involving student information.

sections.body: Operations systems hold more sensitive student information than many people realize. Transportation systems know where students live and when they are picked up, food service systems know which students qualify for free or reduced price meals, and health and allergy data flows into menu planning. Federal rules limit how free or reduced price meal information can be shared. The problem this idea solves is that privacy review is often skipped for operations tools because their contracts are handled by different offices than instructional ones. Every operations tool that touches student data therefore needs the same protections as instructional tools.
sections.heading: The idea

sections.body: In a school or district, every operations tool that touches student data should carry a signed data privacy agreement, limits on how the vendor uses the data, and clear terms for deleting it. The district's privacy lead should review every contract that involves student information, which closes the gap created when operations contracts are handled by different offices than instructional ones. Location data deserves special care, so access to bus tracking apps should be limited to families of students on each route and to staff who need it. Data should be kept only as long as needed. The text does not give grade band variations for this idea.
sections.heading: How it works in school

sections.body: The text gives no study, figure or finding for this idea, so it rests on practice rather than research. It states as a matter of practice that operations systems hold more sensitive student information than many people realize, and it notes that federal rules limit how free or reduced price meal information can be shared without citing a specific rule or study. The guidance that the district's privacy lead should review every contract involving student information is presented as a recommended practice, not as a research finding. No evidence label is given in the supplied text.
sections.heading: What the evidence says

sections.body: The limits and risks here are that operations contracts are sometimes handled by different offices than instructional ones, so privacy review can be skipped, and that location data can reveal patterns about where students go. Access to bus tracking apps should be limited to families of students on each route and to staff who need it, and data should be kept only as long as needed. The decisions that stay with a person are the privacy lead's review of every contract involving student information, the signing of data privacy agreements, the setting of limits on vendor use of data, and the terms for deleting it. Federal rules also constrain how free or reduced price meal information can be shared, which keeps that decision out of local discretion. Nothing here is legal advice; it describes practice.
